record.what_it_does: Community chat platform; API for bots, messaging, guilds, and OAuth2 user integrations.
record.auth_notes: A bot token (header "Authorization: Bot <token>") covers bot actions in guilds the bot was added to. OAuth2 supports the authorization code grant (PKCE recommended), the implicit grant (prototypes only), and client credentials. OAuth2 is used to act as a user with limited scopes (identify, email, guilds, guilds.join, etc.) and to install the bot via the bot/applications.commands scopes. A multi-user toolkit would use OAuth2 for identity and guild install, then act through the bot token. OAuth2 grants no user-level message read/send, and self-botting with user tokens violates the ToS. Incoming channel webhooks carry a token in the URL and are post-only.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create an app and bot for free in the Developer Portal. No paid plan is needed. Some OAuth scopes are partner-approval only: dm_channels.read, voice, rpc*, identify.premium, and applications.builds.upload. Bots in 100+ guilds must be verified. Privileged intents (GUILD_PRESENCES, GUILD_MEMBERS, MESSAGE_CONTENT) can be toggled freely below that size, but verified apps must be approved for them.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST covers channels, messages, guilds, members, roles, threads, webhooks, interactions, application commands, users, emojis, stickers, scheduled events, entitlements, and more. The Gateway websocket delivers real-time events. There is an official OpenAPI 3.1 spec, in public preview.
record.mcp_notes: Discord hosts a docs-only MCP endpoint at https://docs.discord.com/mcp. It is a Mintlify-style server that searches and retrieves developer docs and has a feedback tool. A GET returns HTTP 405, which fits a POST-only MCP endpoint. It does not wrap the Discord API, so it is not counted as an official product MCP. Product MCP servers are community-built, e.g. SaseQ/discord-mcp, which uses a bot token, plus Workato and other vendor connectors.
record.blocker_notes: The API is open and free but bot-centric. OAuth2 does not give user-level message read/send, so the toolkit acts as a bot that each user must install in their guild. Scaling past 100 guilds requires bot verification, and the MESSAGE_CONTENT, GUILD_MEMBERS and GUILD_PRESENCES intents then need approval. Some scopes, such as dm_channels.read, are partner-only. HTTP webhook events cover only app authorization, entitlements, and lobby/game DMs. Message and guild triggers need a persistent Gateway websocket connection.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials
Some scopes require approval from Discord to use.
Verified bots do not have a maximum number of guilds.
For verified apps (required for apps in 100+ guilds)
After your app is verified, you can request privileged intents within the app's settings within the Developer Portal.
Webhook events are one-way events sent to your app over HTTP to notify you when an event occurred.
This repository contains the public preview of the OpenAPI 3.1 specification for Discord's API.
A MCP server for the Discord integration.

'Verification is required for your app to scale past 100 servers.' Same kind of gate as HubSpot's 25-install cap, so labelled the same way.
